To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the integration of transcriptomic and metabolomic data can specify the system's response; (ii) the integration of time-resolved metabolomic data can further specify the metabolic pathways most affected by a studied treatment; and (iii) the integration of metabolomics and transcriptomic data can be used to predict metabolic flux phenotypes in Chlamydomonads.

we developed and applied a novel method to integrate transcriptomics and time resolved metabolomics data to predict metabolic flux phenotypes and we demonstrated the applicability of the method in the dissection the metabolic response of C. reinhardtii to the rapamycin induced inhibition of TORC1.

the integration of metabolomics and transcriptome data can specify the pathways involved in the response of a biological system to a studied treatment, and that TREM Flux is a novel method for the integration of metabolome and transcriptome data in the context of flux phenotyping.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of constraint based methods for integrating time resolved heterogeneous data and the refinement of the predicted flux phenotypes.

the development and validation of methods for integrating transcriptomics and metabolomic data to improve the accuracy of constraint based metabolic network reconstructions and the prediction of flux changes.
the integration of transcriptomic and metabolomic time series data in a constraint based framework.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
TREM Flux is a promising method for the integration of time-resolved metabolomics and transcriptomic data to refine constraint-based flux phenotypes.
the proposed method TREM Flux can be applied in a wide range of systems to integrate time resolved unlabeled data and transcriptomics data for the prediction of the metabolic flux phenotype.
the proposed method TREM Flux can be used to predict flux phenotypes in a system under a certain treatment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
TREM Flux can be used to integrate metabolite concentrations with gene expression levels for the prediction of the metabolic response to a studied stimulus.
TREM Flux is a constraint based method that can specify the metabolic response to a treatment by integrating transcriptomics and metabolite data.

the integration of metabolomics and transcriptomic data in a constraint based approach provides a better understanding of the metabolic response to a studied condition than transcriptomics or metabolomics alone.
The main takeaway from our work is that
metabolomics data can be integrated in the prediction of flux phenotype by constraint based methods.

the integration of transcriptomic, proteomic and metabolomic data is an effective way to specify the metabolic fluxes and to identify key metabolic reactions involved in the system’s response to a studied condition.
the integration of heterogeneous data can provide additional insights into the metabolic response of a cell to a studied treatment.
